title: Callable.is_valid() is unreliable for native static method Callables and breaks Callable.bind()
body:
### Tested versions

* Reproducible in: **Godot Engine v4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf]**
* Not tested: earlier stable versions
* Not tested: development snapshots

Reproduced using an official Godot build without GDExtensions, C++ modules, or editor plugins.

### System information

Godot v4.7.2.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 6900 XT (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.21043.12001) - AMD Ryzen 9 5900X 12-Core Processor (24 threads) - 63.90 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

I found that the result returned by `Callable.is_valid()` is unreliable. A Callable that can actually be called can return `false`.

This seems to happen specifically when `Callable.get_object()` returns a `GDScriptNativeClass` and the target method is static, such as the static methods in `FileAccess`.

```gdscript
var callable: Callable = FileAccess.file_exists
```

This is a Callable that can be called successfully, but `is_valid()` returns `false`.

Then, if we bind an argument to it:

```gdscript
callable.bind("res://icon.svg")
```

the resulting Callable changes from callable to uncallable. Calling `call()` on it produces an error.

I found that the reason is that `Callable::is_valid()` uses the following code:

```cpp
return get_object() && get_object()->has_method(get_method());
```

For a `GDScriptNativeClass` object, `has_method()` returns `false` for this native static method.

However, `Callable::callp()` does not rely on `is_valid()`. Instead, it uses `ClassDB::get_method("FileAccess", "file_exists")` to find the method and execute it. This is why the original Callable can still be called successfully.

After binding arguments, the Callable changes to a custom Callable, so `bound.is_custom() == true`.

At this point, `Callable::callp()` checks `is_valid()` for the custom Callable and reports an error. As a result, the Callable with bound arguments can no longer be called.

My conclusion is that the result of `Callable.is_valid()` is not reliable. It does not accurately reflect whether a Callable can actually be called. Furthermore, this unreliable result causes a Callable that has arguments bound with `bind()` to become uncallable.


### Minimal reproduction project

A minimal reproduction project is attached to this issue.

[mbp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32754909/mbp.zip)
